rules.statement: Elementary-flow classification uses valid controlled category identifiers with continuous levels and no skipped intermediate level.

applicability.scope: Flow datasets whose type is Elementary flow and that provide elementary-flow categorization.

positive: Levels 0, 1, and 2 use identifiers present in the shipped controlled category hierarchy.
negative: A level-2 category is supplied without level 1, or an identifier is absent from the shipped hierarchy.

rules.statement: Every flow-property mean value is a positive real number and the referenced quantitative property has mean value 1.0 relative to itself.

applicability.scope: Every flow-property entry; the 1.0 condition applies to the entry selected by the quantitative reference.

positive: The selected reference property has meanValue 1.0 and every additional property has a positive conversion ratio.
negative: A flow property has meanValue 0, a negative value, or the selected reference property differs from 1.0.

rules.statement: The flow base name uses technical terminology and keeps geography, time, and quantitative qualifiers in their dedicated fields.

positive: The base name identifies the technical flow and records geography in location metadata.
negative: The base name embeds a year or location instead of using the dedicated metadata field.

rules.statement: A flow identifies an existing reference flow-property entry and that entry references the maintained flow-property dataset defining its quantity and unit.

positive: The quantitative reference points to an existing local flow-property ID whose global reference identifies the intended physical quantity.
negative: The quantitative reference points to a missing local ID or the selected property lacks its flow-property dataset reference.

rules.statement: A flow declares exactly one allowed dataset type: Elementary flow, Product flow, or Waste flow.

positive: typeOfDataSet is Product flow and its classification and reference property are consistent with that choice.
negative: typeOfDataSet is absent, custom text, or inconsistent with an elementary-flow categorization.

rules.statement: Every process exchange provides the numerical amount required by the methodology and its applicable amount constraints.

applicability.scope: Every process exchange, using the amount representation applicable to that exchange.

positive: An exchange provides a finite mean amount consistent with its documented unit and source evidence.
negative: An exchange provides no applicable numerical amount or supplies a non-numeric value.

rules.statement: For a single reference Flow, the Process baseName equals the exact reference Flow baseName in each corresponding language; equality does not extend to the complete name object. Multiple-reference names identify all reference flows. Geography and time remain in dedicated metadata fields. Base-name equality alone does not establish Flow compatibility.

applicability.scope: Process datasets with reference flows, including Unit processes, LCI results and partly terminated systems regardless of publication status. A Flow may be shared by multiple Processes. This is TIDAS field-scoped application of ILCD Rule 20, which recommends full-name alignment.

positive: Two compatible Processes share the same exact Alternating current Flow and baseName; their treatmentStandardsRoutes name supported coal and wind technologies separately.
A Process uses the exact Diesel baseName and retains its supported petroleum-refining route in treatmentStandardsRoutes; geography remains metadata.
negative: A multi-functional process omits one reference flow or embeds a year in baseName.
A Process keeps a different baseName for a single reference Flow, or copies the complete Flow name into baseName.
A generic Electricity label is substituted for Alternating current without an identity decision, or base-name equality is used to ignore incompatible Flow route/property qualifiers.

rules.statement: Process-name qualifiers retain established production mix, consumption mix, technology-specific and at/to descriptions, supplemented where needed by evidenced grade/route, supply scope, delivery interface and quantitative specifications. Technology-specific is valid on its own and may coexist with a documented mix; enterprise procurement mix is an optional TIDAS extension. Production mix uses a documented weighting basis within a defined geographic and temporal scope. Retain the established availability/handover and transport-to-node meanings without inferring complete inventory coverage. Separate physical supply from contractual attributes. Preserve meaningful descriptors in every authored language; exclude functional-unit amounts, conversion boilerplate, footprint results and supplier weights. A Model-derived resulting Process retains the reviewed whole-Model name.

applicability.scope: Process datasets that have the corresponding qualifier information.

positive: A production mix qualifier is placed in mixAndLocationTypes and a grade standard in treatmentStandardsRoutes, each supported by the actual Process.
A supported 12-hour nitrate-storage descriptor is moved from baseName into treatmentStandardsRoutes without losing it in either authored language.

A Model combines compatible diesel supplies and transport to the consumer: its name reflects that whole supply boundary, and the resulting Process keeps that Model name instead of inheriting only a final refinery's route and plant-gate boundary.
A supported sulfur mass fraction distinguishes a diesel specification in functionalUnitFlowProperties; an absent optional quantitative qualifier stays empty.

Technology-specific remains a valid standalone mixAndLocationTypes descriptor; a documented technology-specific production mix can also combine it with Production mix, while the specific route remains in treatmentStandardsRoutes.

An electricity mapping adapter names its actually evidenced availability point without inferring consumption mix or a transport boundary; it does not require a to qualifier merely because the output reaches a user.

Where established descriptions are insufficient, an evidenced enterprise procurement mix is an optional TIDAS supplement; scope, supplier weights and contractual accounting are documented rather than placed in quantitative product properties.

Production mix, at plant; Consumption mix, to consumer; and Technology-specific, to wholesale remain valid established examples when their stated boundaries are supported. Chinese production mix may retain 生产组合 or 生产混合, and consumption mix may retain 消费组合 or 消费混合; none requires bulk terminology replacement. At wholesale and at point-of-sale also retain their availability/handover meaning; transport and inventory coverage are checked separately.
The S355 grade remains in treatmentStandardsRoutes despite its digits; an evidenced 30 % recycled material by mass of finished product belongs in functionalUnitFlowProperties with that basis.
negative: A location/mix qualifier is placed in treatmentStandardsRoutes or all qualifiers are flattened into baseName.
Generic shared-Flow qualifiers overwrite a supported Process route, or renaming silently loses a descriptor in one authored language.
An unreviewed production route or global average placeholder, a 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ conversion identity, or reference-amount scaling instructions are used as product qualifiers.
A Model with mixed supplies and transport is named after a narrower final Process without checking the whole-Model evidence.
Delivery to a consumer, a reference Flow labelled consumption mix, a grid-loss proxy or a mapping adapter is treated as sufficient evidence for consumption mix.

A supported Technology-specific descriptor is rejected, all Consumption mix names are forced to become Market consumption mix, or enterprise procurement mix is required universally or presented as an original ILCD class or market-representative supply without evidence.

At/to is universally redefined as before/after node processing, a to boundary is claimed without transport evidence, or a delivery node alone is used to claim complete cradle-to-node inventory coverage; a certificate is used to claim physical generation technology or zero impact.

A grade number is moved into quantitative properties, a supplier procurement share is called recycled-material content, or 1 kg, 1 kWh, a footprint result or supplier weights fill functionalUnitFlowProperties.

rules.statement: The process dataset version uses fixed-width NN.NN notation with an optional three-digit development component (NN.NN.NNN) and increases when content changes.

applicability.scope: Every versioned process dataset; monotonic comparison applies when a previous published version exists.

positive: 01.02 and 01.02.003 both satisfy the Version schema; 01.02.003 follows 01.02 after a content change.
negative: 1.1, 01.02.03, or a version not greater than the previous published version.
